input: This executive summary presents an overview of a proposed heat-recovery retrofit at a food plant, where refrigeration operations currently consume a total of 2202 MWh of electricity per year. According to projections provided by the equipment vendor, the retrofit is expected to save 15% of that annual use, which corresponds to a derived saving of 330 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the project is $472k, and at an electricity price of $0.14 per kWh the derived annual saving amounts to $46k, which in turn leads to a derived simple payback period of 10.3 years. It is important to note, however, that the saving figure is a vendor projection and has not been measured at this plant, and it should also be noted that the refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled as part of this assessment, which means that a degree of uncertainty inevitably remains around the projected figures. Put in trade-off terms, the derived annual saving of $46k stands against a capital cost of $472k, and the relationship between the two figures is what produces the derived simple payback of 10.3 years quoted above, on the assumptions that have been stated. In light of these considerations, it is recommended that a metered trial be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, so that measured data can be obtained in order to inform the final investment decision. The plant engineer will be responsible for owning and overseeing the trial.
target: The recommendation is a metered trial of the heat-recovery retrofit on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision. The plant engineer owns the trial. Refrigeration at the plant is a continuous load, and the heat the refrigeration system rejects is at present discharged rather than recovered, which is the situation the retrofit addresses. The food plant uses 2202 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, and the equipment vendor projects that the retrofit will save 15% of that use, a derived saving of 330 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $472k. At an electricity price of $0.14 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $46k and the derived simple payback is 10.3 years: the retrofit returns $46k per year against a capital cost of $472k. The saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the payback rests on a projected saving and on a load profile with the peak month missing. The trial replaces the projection with a measured saving on a single line. A measured figure at that scale either supports the vendor figure or shows the gap between the projection and the plant, and the capital decision is taken on the measured result rather than on the projection. The payback of 10.3 years is long enough that the difference between the projected saving and a measured saving decides the case, which is the reason the trial comes before the capital decision and not after it. The trial also fixes the scope of any later decision: a retrofit beyond the trialled line is a separate decision, taken on the trial result and on the load profile with the missing peak month supplied.
